Q: How does React Router v7 choose between two equally specific matching routes? A:

React Router v7 uses ranked route matching, and in this specific tie-breaking case, the rule is:

\> Static segments score higher than dynamic (`:param`) segments at the same position.

For your two routes:

| Segment | `/foo/:someVar/baz` | `/foo/bar/:someOtherVar` |

|---|---|---|

| 1 | `foo` (static) | `foo` (static) |

| 2 | `:someVar` ❌ dynamic | `bar` ✅ static ← **wins here** |

| 3 | `baz` (static) | `:someOtherVar` dynamic |

React Router compares segments **left to right**, and at segment 2, `bar` (static) beats `:someVar` (dynamic). So **`/foo/bar/:someOtherVar` wins** — `<B />` will render with `{ someOtherVar: "baz" }`.

The simple priority rule:

```

static segment > dynamic (:param) > wildcard (*)

```

Important: Declaration order does not matter in v7. Unlike React Router v5, routing is score-based even if you define Route A first, Route B wins because of higher specificity at segment 2.

So for URL `/foo/bar/baz`, the answer to your questions:

1. `<B />` renders (route `/foo/bar/:someOtherVar`)

2. The tie is resolved by static vs dynamic comparison at the first differing segment

Q: Building a custom "lda" object in R A:

The short answer is "yes", it is possible to build an "lda" object with custom parameters without passing through the lda() function, but if you want to create one then you need a function that will create a list that has all the same members as the "lda" object ("prior", "counts", "means", "scaling", "lev", "svd", "N", "call", "terms", and "xlevels") and give it the class "lda".

The only purpose I can see in doing this is so that you still have access to the generic LDA methods (coef(), model.frame(), pairs(), plot(), predict() and print()), but even here you would have to make sure that the generic methods make sense in light of your own method.

Given that, it may make more sense to just create your own LDA class and write its own generic methods.

It's impossible to know from the question exactly what you are trying to do, what you have done already and what might be the best route for you to take. Perhaps you could explain a bit more about what your extra parameters are trying to achieve, how you currently use them in your LDA calculation, and why you think having the output as a MASS::lda object would be useful to you?
